subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who became indistinguishable from Zuggtmoy’s rot, and was looted with efficient respect after her theological problem was resolved.
source_quote: So I looted her with the efficient respect one extends to a theological problem that has been resolved.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth subverted by Zuggtmoy, whose prayer book documented a slow, ambiguous corruption through marginalia in a second handwriting.
source_quote: The marginalia told the story... Two hands because two minds had been working the same pen.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin had his tooth collected as a trophy by Ilvara, and reclaimed it from her confiscated belongings after recognizing its significance.
source_quote: Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back. He held it for a moment without saying anything.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym sent frantic sealed orders seeking Ilvara’s whereabouts, unaware she had been consumed by Zuggtmoy’s influence and ceased responding.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing... Didn't you read the previous memo?

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove attempted political correspondence with Ilvara, but the communication failed because she had been pulled away by Zuggtmoy’s influence.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else.

subject: theological corruption of Ilvara
fact: Ilvara’s prayer book revealed a gradual theological corruption by Zuggtmoy, documented in marginalia that shifted from formal liturgy to associative, unstable writing.
source_quote: The early entries were neat and formal... then, gradually, around the margins, a second voice crept in.

subject: discovery of Zuggtmoy-Lolth theological treatise
fact: A sealed wax pouch contained a meticulously written theological treatise arguing that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same entity, a conclusion reached through backward reasoning.
source_quote: It's basically a long theological exploration of why Zuggtmoy and Lolth — and claiming that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same thing.

subject: Drow Outpost
fact: The Drow Outpost was looted of personal, theological, and material artifacts that documented the descent of its occupants into Zuggtmoy’s influence.
source_quote: A cleric's catalogue of the things a high priestess of Lolth becomes when something older and stranger finds the seam in her theology and begins to work.

subject: wax pouch
fact: The wax pouch contained a theological treatise arguing the identity of Lolth and Zuggtmoy, written in close, careful script by a mind unraveling toward madness.
source_quote: Inside were pages of close, careful script — the handwriting of someone who had once been methodical.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book was a standard Lolth devotional text, but its margins contained a second, increasingly unstable handwriting that documented her subversion by Zuggtmoy.
source_quote: The marginalia told the story... Someone else had written in her prayer book. Or — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: Living Serpent Head Scourge
fact: The Living Serpent Head Scourge was a weapon whose head was a sentient or partially animate serpent, preserved as a museum-grade artifact of terrible craftsmanship.
source_quote: It sounds like a great museum piece... You document them. You label them carefully. You do not pretend they aren't what they are.

subject: Drow cloak (spider-silk)
fact: A fine spider-silk Drow cloak, capable of drinking shadow, was taken from Asha Vandree’s body and claimed by Zalthir.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow.

subject: flask of Overbright brandy
fact: A flask of Overbright brandy was received with personal interest, distinct from other looted items due to its intimate, sensory appeal.
source_quote: The flask of Overbright brandy I received with considerably more personal interest.

subject: water-damaged prisoner journal
fact: A water-damaged journal from an unnamed prisoner contained legible handwriting that showed the writer had kept records until they could no longer.
source_quote: The pages were swollen and the ink had run in places, but the handwriting was still visible in the drier sections.

subject: origin of Ilvara’s corruption
fact: The source of Ilvara’s subversion remains unknown — whether induced by another entity or self-initiated through altered consciousness — and the ambiguity is deeply troubling.
source_quote: I could not tell from the text whether she had known she wasn't resisting or whether she had genuinely believed she was still moving in her own direction.

subject: identity of the marginalia writer
fact: It is unclear whether the second handwriting in Ilvara’s prayer book was her own altered self or an external influence, leaving the nature of her corruption unresolved.
source_quote: Someone else had written in her prayer book. Or — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: theological implications of Lolth-Zuggtmoy unity
fact: The treatise claiming Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same entity challenges the foundations of drow theology and may represent a new, dangerous heresy.
source_quote: It was very well-argued. It was also completely mad.

subject: session date
fact: The events occurred during a looting operation at a Drow Outpost, following the deaths of Ilvara and Asha Vandree, and the discovery of their corrupted artifacts.
source_quote: Asha Vandree's body was next... The last item was on Ilvara herself.
